writer_followup.probe_correction: The original NOWAIT probe returned rows on both old and changed source because that distinct lock mode is not enforced; it is not valid unchanged-UPDATE red evidence. The Go versus a7eb7f20 live competing UPDATE and the corrected normal-lock regression are the evidence. The embedded timeout takes about 20 seconds despite SET innodb_lock_wait_timeout=1; per-session timeout propagation is not proven.

live_passed.ownership: Both Go and Rust expose one committed binding before and after caller rollback; the writer sees its staged user value 21 while the peer sees committed value 20, and rollback restores 20
live_passed.shared_lock: Go holding the builtin row blocks Rust CREATE; Rust holding the same row blocks Go CREATE; each command commits one live binding after release
live_passed.unchanged_update: Rust no-op UPDATE holds the matched user row against Go UPDATE until rollback; probe leaves both user rows unchanged
live_passed.cleanup: Probe-created databases were dropped; binding deletion follows Go's tombstone lifecycle; user-data test transactions were rolled back

mixed_workloads.interpretation: All 18 measured TPC-C samples accepted 10000 transactions each, plus six 1000-transaction warmups. Median improvements are +1.8% sysbench, +5.5% two-client TPC-C, +9.1% eight-client TPC-C. Host activity, timing drift, shared evolving data and time-seeded workload RNG prevent a statistical or broad-goal completion claim.

global_command_gap.interpretation: Committed storage, not the point-get binding flag, proves transaction ownership. Go has one committed binding during and after the caller's rollback; Rust has zero. Both preserve the caller's staged data until rollback.
global_command_gap.next_fix: Persist global commands through their own pessimistic transaction, serialize with the shared builtin bind-info row as Go does, then refresh the committed image. Do not commit or reuse the caller's transaction.
global_command_gap.cleanup: Only probe-created databases and bindings were removed; Go owns the normal tombstone GC
